documents.title: Framework agreement contracts - Welding and muffing district heating
documents.text:
Title: Framework agreement contracts - Welding and muffing district heating.
Category: Norway – District-heating mains construction work – Framework agreement contracts - Welding and muffing district heating.
Notice type: Contract award notice 680501-2026.
Buyer: LYSE NEO AS (NO).
Winner: West-team AS (NO).
Total value: 19235075 NOK.
Published: 2026-10-02.
CPV: 45232140, 45231110.
Description: The procurement is for a framework agreement for contract work in the form of welding and muffing of district heating pipes (fv-pipes). As a part of district heating development, the contracting authority has, in periods, a need for extra capacity. Typical work assignments that are included in this contract (not exhaustively, other assignments can occur): · Welding on county road pipes in the dimensions up to and including DN250 · Muffing on county road pipes in dimensions up to and including Ø 450 mm. The work place will be on the Contracting Authority's projects/sites in Nord-Jæren. Most of the contracting authority ́s district heating installations are located in Stavanger, Sandnes and Sola municipalities. The work will mainly take place outside in ditches in urban areas. Project work connected to district heating will mainly be carried out by the Contracting Authority's own installers/welders. The Contracting Authority can, however, use the Supplier for welding and movable work on district heating pipes at periods with many assignments and high activity. When working in ditches that can contain a lot of existing infrastructure, it can often be challenging to plan progress in a structured and rational way. The tenderer must expect to move between different projects, i.e. building and construction sites, within the working day/work period that each Call-off applies to. There may also be instances where the tenderer must move within a project during the work day. The tenderer's personnel will be managed/led by the Contracting Authority's project manager and the Contracting Authority presents the necessary material and work basis/drawings.

documents.title: KPIL wins over ₹4,000 crore gas pipeline EPC order in UAE
documents.text:
KPIL wins over ₹4,000 crore gas pipeline EPC order in UAE
ETEnergyWorld Desk
Published On Sep 28, 2026 at 10:59 AM IST
Read by
100 Professionals
Gas pipelines (Image for representation)Kalpataru Projects International Limited (KPIL) on Monday said it secured a 'major' international contract for an engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) gas pipeline project in the United Arab Emirates, valued over ₹4,000 crore.According to an exchange filing, the Mumbai-headquartered infrastructure major received a formal Letter of Award for the project in the normal course of business.The company classifies contracts with an estimated value exceeding ₹4,000 crore as ‘major’ orders.Manish Mohnot, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of KPIL, said the prestigious overseas win reinforces the company's proven execution credentials and track record in the global oil and gas space, calling it a testament to its technical expertise, operational delivery, and growing international scale.
Advt
KPIL's latest reported order book stood at ₹66,607 crore as of June 30, 2026, its highest ever. The company has recorded FY27 year-to-date order inflows of more than ₹7,668 crore and had an additional approximately ₹7,300 crore of L1/favourably placed orders.KPIL’s FY27 order inflows have been led by T&D and Buildings & Factories, which together accounted for 91 per cent of year-to-date inflows. Management is targeting FY27 order inflows of around ₹30,000 crore, with the possibility of revising this guidance upward by the end of Q2 FY27.Meanwhile, just days earlier, on September 25, KPIL announced the successful listing of its Swedish step-down subsidiary, Linjemontage i Grästorp AB, on the Nasdaq Stockholm exchange under the ticker symbol LMGAB.The transaction made KPIL the first Indian company to list a foreign subsidiary on the Swedish bourse. The initial share sale was priced at SEK 46 per equity share, valuing Linjemontage at SEK 2,357 million.Following the listing, KPIL retains an approximate 65.9 per cent ownership interest in the Swedish power infrastructure company through its wholly owned subsidiary, Kalpataru Power Transmission Sweden AB, which is slated to receive gross proceeds of approximately SEK 711.5 million, including the green shoe option, subject to customary issue expenses and adjustments.
